As with everything, it's complicated. In general, 223 will feel a lot more like a 22lr than a shotgun. In fact, the weight of the projectile is actually pretty close between a 223 and a 22lr even though the 223 has much more powder. On average the 223 projectile is about 20% heavier, but you can find ammo with the 223 projectile being lighter than 22lr projectile. A 10-gauge can easily weight 10-15x as much as 223 or 22lr. There are several different gauges of shotguns, so a 410 is going to have way less kickback than a 10-gauge.

Another part of the equation is the weight of the weapon. ARs are intended to fire much more rounds at higher pressure (more powder). Therefore, ARs tend to be heavy for both structural integrity and heat dissapation. The heavier a weapon is, the less kickback it will experience.

In summary, a 223 will have slightly more kickback that a 22lr but much less than a 10-gauge. In my subjective opinion, the 223 is louder than a 10-gauge and the 22lr is downright quiet. All of this is dependent up the weapon system and ammo used. I find 223 and 22lr enjoyable to shoot for 100s of rounds, but I double my hearing protection when firing the 223 a lot. I don't enjoy shooting a 10-gauge for more than about 20 rounds.
